## Summary

Add a new "Step 0: Work-item audit gate" to the cleanup skill instructions (`skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`) that invokes the audit skill when the current branch has an associated work-item ID, before any branch operations begin.

## Context

The cleanup skill currently has no awareness of work-item lifecycle. This step gates the cleanup process on a work-item audit: if the branch has an associated work item, the audit skill is invoked first. The existing audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) produces structured verdicts (`met`/`unmet`/`partial`) that the agent uses to decide whether to proceed or abort.

This is a SKILL.md-only change — agent behavior instructions, no Python code changes.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (insert new Step 0 before current Step 1)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new "Step 0" is added before the existing Step 1 in `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`
2. Step 0 instructs the agent to: check the `work_item_id` field from the `inspect_current_branch.py` JSON output, invoke the audit skill if an ID is found, and proceed or abort based on audit results
3. The step documents the decision rules: all criteria `met` -> proceed; any `unmet`/`partial` -> abort; no acceptance criteria defined -> abort
4. Existing steps 1-9 remain unchanged in behavior and order
5. Step 0 is skipped when no work-item ID is found (e.g., on `main` or branches without tokens)

## Minimal Implementation

- Insert a new section in SKILL.md before the current "1. Inspect current branch"
- Reference the audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) invocation pattern
- Document the decision rule: only proceed if every criterion has verdict `met`
- Document the skip logic when no work-item ID is present in the `inspect_current_branch.py` output

## Note

This task covers the audit gate structure. The status transition (on pass) and abort messaging (on failure) are covered by sibling tasks but may be implemented together since they all modify the same Step 0 section.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`
data.title: Add audit gate step to cleanup skill

## Summary

Document in the cleanup skill instructions that when the audit passes (all criteria `met`), the agent should transition the work item to `status=completed, stage=in_review` and add a comment before proceeding with branch cleanup.

## Context

This follows the same transition pattern established by SA-0ML7OP7L40QKWDB1 (implement-flow: mark work-item completed/in_review after merge). Consistency with that pattern ensures downstream processes (triage audit, producer review) work correctly.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (additions to Step 0, after audit pass condition)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. SKILL.md Step 0 includes explicit `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` command to run after audit passes
2. The transition uses the same pattern as the implement-flow (SA-0ML7OP7L40QKWDB1): status=completed, stage=in_review
3. A comment is added to the work item documenting that cleanup audit passed, including branch name context: `wl comment add <id> --comment "Cleanup audit passed on branch <branch-name>. Work item transitioned to in_review." --author <agent-name>`
4. The transition happens after the audit passes but before any branch operations begin (i.e., before Step 1)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add transition instructions to Step 0 in SKILL.md after the audit-pass decision point
- Include the exact `wl update` and `wl comment add` commands the agent should run
- Specify that this must happen before proceeding to Step 1

## Note

This modifies the same Step 0 section as the sibling audit-gate and abort-behavior tasks. The implementer may combine all three into a single commit.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (additions to Step 0)

data.description:
## Summary

Define clear abort messaging in the cleanup skill for when the audit gate fails (criteria `unmet`/`partial`) or when no acceptance criteria are defined on the work item.

## Context

When the audit gate determines that cleanup should not proceed, the agent needs clear instructions on what to output and how to halt. There are two abort scenarios:
1. **Criteria unmet/partial:** The audit skill returns one or more criteria with `unmet` or `partial` verdicts.
2. **No acceptance criteria:** The work item has no acceptance criteria section defined, so the audit cannot verify completion.

Both scenarios result in a hard abort — no branch operations are performed.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (abort behavior in Step 0)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When any criterion is `unmet` or `partial`, the agent outputs a clear message listing which criteria failed and their verdicts (referencing the audit report)
2. When no acceptance criteria are defined on the work item, the agent outputs a message explaining that the work item cannot be verified and cleanup is aborted
3. After abort, no branch operations are performed (steps 1-9 are all skipped entirely)
4. The abort message suggests next steps (e.g., "Fix the unmet criteria and re-run cleanup" or "Add acceptance criteria to the work item and re-run cleanup")

## Minimal Implementation

- Add abort message templates/examples to Step 0 in SKILL.md
- Document the "no acceptance criteria" abort case as a separate condition
- Document explicitly that the agent must not proceed to any subsequent step after abort
- Include example abort output for both scenarios

## Note

This modifies the same Step 0 section as the sibling audit-gate and status-transition tasks. The implementer may combine all three into a single commit.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (abort behavior in Step 0)

Summary: Implement 'wl ampa config' subcommand providing show (default), set <key> <value>, and reset <key> with validation of keys.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'wl ampa config' prints each config field, its effective value, and the source (env / persisted / default).
- 'wl ampa config set <key> <value>' persists overrides to scheduler_store.json and validates keys; unknown keys are rejected with a clear error.
- 'wl ampa config reset <key>' removes persisted overrides for that key.
- CLI operations respect local-operator-only constraints (file permissions / user ownership).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add subcommand in ampa/scheduler_cli.py following existing CLI pattern.
- Implement validation using SchedulerConfig fields.
- Persist via helper from Feature 1 and trigger SIGHUP on set/reset.
- Add unit tests for CLI parsing and persistence behavior.

## Deliverables
CLI code, tests, help text, docs update.

Summary: Extend command entries with allowed_hours and allowed_days, store windows in UTC, accept/validate ranges (including cross-midnight), and skip commands outside windows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Command schema includes allowed_hours (e.g., ['9-10','22-2']) and allowed_days (e.g., ['mon-fri']).
- Scheduler selection logic silently skips commands that are currently outside their window.
- Windows are accepted in local timezone on input, stored in UTC, and displayed in local timezone.
- Tests cover cross-midnight windows and DST boundary cases.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add fields to CommandSpec and SchedulerStore handling in ampa/scheduler.py.
- Implement parser for hour and day ranges and integrate checks into selection loop.
- Add unit tests for parsing and evaluation; integration test for skipping commands outside window.

## Deliverables
code changes, tests, schema doc update (ampa/scheduler_schema.md).

Summary: Add a SIGHUP handler in the scheduler daemon that reloads scheduler_store.json immediately so wl ampa config set takes effect without waiting for the next poll.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Daemon installs a SIGHUP handler which reloads the store and new config atomically.
- CLI set/reset signals the running daemon (using existing PID file if present; otherwise a well-known pidfile).
- Reload does not interrupt in-progress runs (only changes selection criteria).
- Tests simulate SIGHUP and validate reload behavior.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add SIGHUP handler in ampa/daemon.py (or scheduler entrypoint) to call the store reload path.
- Update wl ampa config CLI to locate the scheduler PID (existing pidfile or well-known runtime pidfile).
- Add tests to assert in-memory config updates after SIGHUP.

## Deliverables
daemon signal handler, CLI signal code, tests, docs for operator flow.

## Audit Test Suite Refactoring

**Summary:** Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to target the new descriptor-driven handler API. Add new test files for `AuditResult` dataclass/parser and handler unit tests. Maintain coverage for cooldown (caller concern), blocked items, Discord integration, and auto-completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Existing 13 test scenarios from `tests/test_triage_audit.py` are preserved or intentionally replaced with equivalent coverage targeting the new handler API
- [ ] New tests for `AuditResult` parsing (>=5 samples: pass, fail, malformed, empty, multi-AC)
- [ ] New tests for each handler covering: from-state validation, invariant evaluation, state transitions, error cases
- [ ] New tests for extended auto-completion checks (PR merge, CI status, PR comments, children, deps)
- [ ] All external calls mocked (`wl`, `opencode run`, `gh pr view`, `gh api`)
- [ ] Test coverage for audit-related code paths >= prior level as measured by `pytest --cov`
- [ ] Tests verify behavioral parity with descriptor definitions (not hardcoded heuristics)

## Minimal Implementation

- Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to target new handler functions/classes
- New `tests/test_audit_result.py` for AuditResult dataclass and parser
- New `tests/test_audit_handlers.py` for handler-specific unit tests (if not covered by refactored file)
- Update mocking patterns to match new API (protocols, adapters)

## Dependencies

- SA-0MM8W4FQR0UY1NHQ (AuditResult dataclass)
- SA-0MM8W553C1WK7JE5 (audit_result handler)
- SA-0MM8W5EXT1BXC7PB (audit_fail handler)
- SA-0MM8W5U8C0QGGXTD (close_with_audit handler)
- SA-0MM8W69L91DJQY50 (routing — partial block for integration tests only)

## Deliverables

- Refactored test files
- New test files as needed
- Coverage report verification

## Reference Files

- `tests/test_triage_audit.py` — existing tests (1178 lines, 13 tests)
- `docs/workflow/test-plan.md` — TC-DL test specifications for audit scenarios
- `docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md` — audit failure flow reference

data.description:
# Reduce audit skill initial session context size

## Headline

Every `pi` subprocess spawned by the audit skill loads ~49KB (~12.3K tokens) of static context at session start — 40KB of it is a byte-identical AGENTS.md loaded twice (global + project) plus a ~7KB skills section — for prompts that are fully self-contained and never use either. Adding `--no-context-files --no-skills` to the runner's pi invocation cuts per-call static context by ~96% (~49KB → ~2KB).

## Problem statement

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` spawns many `pi -p --mode json` subprocess calls per audit (Phase 1 parent + N child screenings, Phase 2 deep + N child analyses, plus recursively auto-triggered child audits — 8 call sites, several in per-child loops). Each fresh pi session starts with a large static context:

| Component | Size | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (global) | 20,086 B | Always loaded by `loadProjectContextFiles()` |
| `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` | 20,086 B | Loaded from ancestor chain — **byte-identical to global** (verified `diff`) |
| `<available_skills>` XML block | ~7,130 B | 17 skills; injected whenever `read` tool available (all audit calls use `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls`) |
| Base system prompt | ~2,000 B | Fixed |
| **Total** | **~49,300 B ≈ 12.3K tokens** | per pi call |

A typical audit with a few children = 10–14 pi calls → **~150K tokens of pure startup overhead per audit**, repeated for every audit run. Session logs confirm the volume: audit-skill sessions grow to 0.5–0.8 MB each, and ~4,300 session files exist.

Crucially, the audit prompts are **fully self-contained**: they carry the read-only mandate, JSON output format, FILE SCOPE manifest, SCANNING block, and criteria (verified at call sites ~L2435, ~L2729, ~L3390). They never reference AGENTS.md workflow instructions (worktree lifecycle, implement skill, wl CRUD procedures) or the skills section — that content is irrelevant to a JSON-only, read-only model, and the workflow instructions could even conflict with the audit's read-only mandate.

## Users

- **Release operators / audit model operators** — audits become cheaper, faster, and less likely to hit token limits on large work items.
- **The pi Local Proxy / model backend** — less input-token load per call across the N+1 audit fan-out.

User story: *As a release operator, I want audit pi sessions to start with minimal static context so each of the many per-audit model calls is fast, cheap, and within token limits.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_call_pi()` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` adds `--no-context-files` and `--no-skills` to the pi command for both `enable_tools=True` and `enable_tools=False` paths; unit tests assert the flags are present in the constructed command.
2. Measurable context goal: across a random sampling of **5 re-audited work items**, each audit pi session starts with **fewer than 10K input tokens** of static context (previously ~12.3K tokens per call); verified by capturing each sampled session's initial context/token usage. (Expected static context after the change: ~2KB ≈ 500 tokens; the 10K ceiling is the hard AC bound.)
3. Verdict spot-check: the same random sampling of 5 work items is re-audited and yields **the same verdicts before and after** the change (no verdict regressions).
4. Full audit test suite passes (`skill/audit/tests/`).
5. `skill/audit/SKILL.md` scripts section documents that pi calls run with context/skills disabled and why (prompts are self-contained).

## Constraints

- Audit prompts must remain self-contained — no prompt may start depending on AGENTS.md content that `-nc` now removes. (Currently none do; this is an invariant to preserve.)
- Verdict semantics unchanged; the runner's two-phase pipeline and status lifecycle must not be altered.
- `-nc`/`-ns` are loader toggles, compatible with `--mode json` and `--tools`.

## Existing state

- `_call_pi()` builds `cmd = [pi_bin, "-p", "--mode", "json", "--model", model, prompt]` (+ `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls --exclude-tools ask_question` when `enable_tools=True`). No context-reduction flags are passed.
- pi provides `--no-context-files`/`-nc` and `--no-skills`/`-ns` CLI toggles (verified in `dist/cli/args.js`).
- Tests already assert command construction by mocking `Popen` (`test_audit_runner.py` ~L295–370, concurrency tests) — new flags are testable the same way.

## Desired change

1. In `_call_pi()`, append `--no-context-files --no-skills` to `cmd` (alongside the existing `enable_tools` block).
2. Add unit tests asserting both flags present in both tool modes.
3. Add a `# Context reduction` note in `_call_pi`'s docstring and a short paragraph in `SKILL.md` scripts section.
4. (Optional, low priority) `--no-session` to stop writing ~0.5–0.8 MB session files per call; consider separately as it changes debuggability.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** `-nc` removes all AGENTS.md guidance; if a future prompt relies on it, the model loses instructions. **Mitigation:** prompts are currently self-contained; AC 1/5 keeps this explicit and documented. Only tool-enabled calls read files, driven by FILE SCOPE, not AGENTS.md.
- **Risk:** `-ns` removes skill descriptions; audit prompts never invoke skills. **Mitigation:** verified — no skill references in audit prompts.
- **Assumption:** the two AGENTS.md files are meant to be identical (project copy mirrors global). If not, deduplication at the file level is out of scope; the runner flag works regardless.
- **Scope-creep risk:** de-duplicating AGENTS.md globally, adding `--no-session`, or trimming prompt content (see P11, SA-0MSF4AFX9007INSP — completed) are separate items, not part of this change.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi()` (~L1040–1075) builds the pi command; add the flags here. `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` (~L2143) forwards; docstrings updated.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — command-construction tests (~L286–372) extended for the new flags.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — scripts section documents the flags.
- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` + `projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` — the duplicated 20KB context files (root cause; not changed here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MSF4AFX9007INSP` — Audit skill: trim prompt size — summarize auto-appended related-work report in child/parent prompts (P11). **Completed.** Complementary: reduces *prompt* content; this item reduces *static system context*.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2: performance evaluation and improvement. **Completed.** Parent of the performance work; this item is a further lever.
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7). **Completed.** Prior wall-clock reduction; context reduction stacks with it.
- `SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL` — Audit concurrency limit. **Completed.** Related to per-call cost economics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What makes up the initial context, and where does the duplication come from?" — Answer (analysis): pi's `loadProjectContextFiles()` always loads the global `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` AND walks the ancestor chain from cwd. The project AGENTS.md is byte-identical to the global (verified via `diff`, both 20,086 B), so 40KB of the same content is sent. Skills (~7KB) are appended whenever the `read` tool is available. Source: code inspection of `dist/core/resource-loader.js`, `dist/core/system-prompt.js`, `dist/core/skills.js`; `diff` of the two AGENTS.md files; session-log inspection under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.
- Q: "Are the audit prompts dependent on AGENTS.md or skills content?" — Answer (analysis): No. All Phase 1/Phase 2/project prompts are self-contained (read-only mandate, JSON format, FILE SCOPE manifest, SCANNING block, criteria). Source: `audit_runner.py` prompt construction at L2435, L2729, L3390; session log first-message inspection.
- Q: "Which skills invoke pi subprocesses with the same pattern?" — Answer (analysis): Only `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`. Implement/plan/others do not spawn the pi binary (they run through the harness). Source: grep of `~/.pi/agent/skills/*/scripts/*.py` for pi subprocess invocations.

# Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill

## Problem statement

Every skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, ship, etc.) currently ends its session with an ad-hoc, inconsistently formatted summary. Producers must re-scan raw output to extract status, acceptance-criteria verdicts, and next actions. This work standardizes the end-of-session report into a single, quickly scannable format produced by a shared helper skill that other skills call.

## Users

- **Producers/operators** who review the end of every skill session and need to quickly scan: what was done, are acceptance criteria met, what state is the work item in, what actions (if any) are required of them.
- **Agents/skills** that need a canonical, reusable report template with deterministic metadata (avoiding each skill inventing its own format).

### User stories

- As a producer, I want every skill session to end with the same report structure, so I can scan results quickly without re-reading raw session output.
- As a skill author, I want a helper skill that provides the canonical report template and metadata (type, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, children, audit), so my skill produces compliant reports with minimal effort.
- As a producer, I want to see the acceptance criteria with per-criterion met/unmet verdicts, so I can tell at a glance whether the work item is ready.
- As a producer, I want an explicit "Producer Actions" section, so I know exactly what (if anything) I need to do next.
- As a producer, I want a freeform Notes section, so the agent can surface context, caveats, or assumptions that don't fit the structured sections.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new helper skill (e.g., `skill/report/` or `skill/session-report/`) exists with a SKILL.md defining the canonical end-of-session report format exactly as specified: header `# Completed <skill_name>`, work-item title + id, headline summary, `## Acceptance Criteria` table, `## Meta-Data`, `## Producer Actions`, `## Notes`, `## Conclusion`.
- [ ] The report template matches the requested layout: AC rows are `|<ac#>|<Description>|<Metric>|<met|unmet>|`; Meta-Data lists Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit each as `<icon> <text>`; Producer Actions defaults to `None needed`; Notes is freeform; Conclusion states `<This completes the <skill_name> process for <id> (<title>). Ready for <next_action>.`
- [ ] The report includes the `## Notes` section between `## Producer Actions` and `## Conclusion` for freeform agent commentary.
- [ ] Meta-Data values (Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit) are populated deterministically from the work item (via `wl show <id> --json`), so the report reflects the current worklog state rather than the agent's memory.
- [ ] **Icon mappings match the canonical ContextHub set** (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`, the set used by the `wl` CLI itself): priority 🚨/⭐/📋/🐢, status 🔓/🔄/✔️/⛔/🗑️/💬, stage 💡/📥/📋/🛠️/🔍/🏁, risk 🌱/⚠️/🔥/🚨, effort 🐜/🐇/🐕/🐘/🐋, audit ✅/❌/❔, with bracketed text fallbacks (`[CRIT]`, `[OPEN]`, `[IDEA]`, `[LOW]`, `[XS]`, `[YES]`, etc.) when icons are unavailable. The helper documents the full mapping table and its ContextHub source so the sets cannot drift. (ContextHub already provides this shared helper — `src/icons.ts` + `docs/icons-design.md` — so no new ContextHub work item is required; see Related work.)
- [ ] The helper skill documents a clear invocation contract (how another skill calls it at the end of its session — e.g., a short embeddable instruction block) that skills embed as their final step.
- [ ] **All existing skills that work on work-items are wired to invoke the helper** at the end of their session, each with its SKILL.md updated to reference the helper: intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, and author-command (any skill whose flow creates/updates work items). Verification: grep across `skill/*/SKILL.md` shows every work-item skill ends with the standardized report instruction.
- [ ] A test validates the report renderer: given a work item + AC verdicts, it produces the expected report structure (sections present, AC table rows, metadata icons/values, defaults for empty fields).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including the new skill's SKILL.md, README, and any references in migrated skills.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The helper skill is invoked by other skills; it does not replace a skill's own workflow or status lifecycle management.
- The report is produced at the end of a skill session; it should not require new work-item state changes beyond what the calling skill already performs.
- Report must remain scannable: prose sections (headline, Notes) are concise; structured sections carry the details.
- Keep it simple: a single template + metadata renderer (script or documented wl command) is sufficient; no orchestration framework.
- Icon mappings are sourced from ContextHub's canonical set — do not invent new icons in individual skills.

## Existing state

- Skills currently end sessions with ad-hoc summaries: e.g., implement closes with `<work-item-id>: <concise-summary> / Work committed to dev`; intake ends with an Objective/AC/Effort-Risk summary; audit has its own persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status`).
- No shared report template or helper skill exists (`grep` for `## Producer Actions` / `## Meta-Data` / `## Conclusion` across `skill/*/SKILL.md` returns nothing).
- Worklog exposes all needed metadata via `wl show <id> --json` (issueType, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, childCount, auditResult/audit status).
- Effort/risk use t-shirt sizes (XS–XL) from `skill/effort-and-risk/references/t-shirt_sizes.json`; risk levels are low/medium/high.
- **ContextHub already provides the canonical icon set**: `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` (spec) and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (TypeScript implementation), consumed by the `wl` CLI (`dist/icons.js`). Mappings cover priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, and producer-review flags, each with emoji + bracketed text fallback + accessible label.
- Skills live in `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional `scripts/` and `tests/`; global install symlinks `~/.pi/agent/skills` → this repo's `skill/` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Desired change

1. Create `skill/report/SKILL.md` (or `skill/session-report/`) defining:
   - The canonical report template (exact section order and layout as specified, including `## Notes` before `## Conclusion`).
   - Icon mappings per Meta-Data field sourced from ContextHub's canonical set (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`), with bracketed text fallbacks.
   - Instructions for populating each section (AC verdicts from the calling skill's own evaluation; Meta-Data from `wl show --json`).
   - A short "how to invoke" contract that other skills embed (e.g., a call-out block to add to a skill's final step).
2. Provide `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (or a documented `wl show` + template recipe) that renders the Meta-Data block deterministically from `wl show <id> --json` — helpers to extract/format metadata, icons (reusing ContextHub mappings), and defaults.
3. Wire the helper into **all** work-item skills: update each `skill/*/SKILL.md` (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) so the final step invokes the standardized report.
4. Add tests (e.g., `skill/report/tests/`) validating the template and metadata rendering.
5. Add an example rendered report in the SKILL.md so agents can copy the pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — new helper skill defining the canonical report format, ContextHub-sourced icon mappings, and invocation contract.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — metadata renderer reading `wl show --json`, reusing ContextHub icon mappings.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — tests for template structure, metadata icons, defaults.
- `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` for every work-item skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) — final step invokes the helper report.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — its existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, AC status table) is the closest precedent; reconcile its end-of-session summary with the new template.

## Related work

- `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` + `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` — **canonical icon set** (priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, producer-review) with emoji + text fallbacks + accessible labels; consumed by the `wl` CLI. The report skill reuses these mappings. (This is the shared helper the requirement asks for — no new ContextHub work item needed.)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status` table, `## Variance Decisions`, `## Children Status`); the closest existing structured-report precedent to reconcile/align with.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — defines risk (low/medium/high) and effort t-shirt (XS–XL) values used in the Meta-Data section.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — example helper skill with scripts + tests + a "compact report" pattern.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — skills' shared status/stage transitions; the report's Status/Stage metadata reflects these.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** wiring the helper into every work-item skill is broad; the requirement is explicit, so all work-item skills are in scope for this item. Skills that do not touch work items (e.g., speak) are excluded.
- **Icon consistency:** icon mappings must come from the ContextHub canonical set (single source of truth) to avoid per-skill divergence; the helper documents the mapping table + source. Unknown values fall back to a neutral marker; icons are decorative — the textual value always accompanies them, so reports remain readable in non-emoji terminals/views.
- **Metadata drift:** report reflects the worklog at render time; if the calling skill changes state after rendering, the report may be stale. Mitigation: render the report as the final step of the session.
- **Audit reconciliation:** audit's existing persisted format differs (it is machine-verified). Its end-of-session summary is reconciled with the template; its persisted machine-verified report format is preserved.
- **Assumption:** Meta-Data is rendered deterministically from worklog where possible; the agent supplies only prose (headline, Notes, Producer Actions, Conclusion next-action).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which skill should be the first adopter / what is the migration scope?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Add an AC that wires the helper into all existing skills that work on work-items." The migration scope is therefore ALL work-item skills, not just 1–2 adopters. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What icon mappings should be used?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Icon mappings should be the same as those used in ../ContextHub. If that project does not have a shared helper you can use then create a work item in that project to do so and make this work item dependent upon it." Research: ContextHub provides the canonical icon set in `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (consumed by the `wl` CLI), covering all Meta-Data fields. No new ContextHub work item is required — the helper references that set. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- Q: "Should the report be persisted (e.g., work-item comment) or stdout only?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: stdout only for v1; persistence as follow-up). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).
- Q: "Should Meta-Data be auto-generated from `wl show --json`?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: yes, via a small renderer script). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).
data.title: Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill

## Summary

The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) crashes with an unhandled `TypeError` in `_map_gaps_to_children` (line ~2930) when a Phase 2 deep-analysis AC result carries `evidence` as a `dict` instead of a string:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "audit_runner.py", line 5343, in <module>
    raise SystemExit(main())
  ...
  File "audit_runner.py", line 2930, in _map_gaps_to_children
    for m in re.finditer(r"([\w./-]+\.\w+)(?::\d+)?", evidence):
TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'dict'
```

`_map_gaps_to_children` does `evidence = r.get("evidence", "") or ""` — a truthy dict passes through unvalidated into `re.finditer`, which requires str/bytes. The runner dies mid-run: no report is persisted, no verdict emitted, and the run is wasted (Phase 1 + Phase 2 deep analysis already consumed ~11 minutes).

discovered-from:LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP

## Reproduction

```bash
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm
python3 /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog
```

The Phase 2 model returned an AC verdict whose `evidence` field is a JSON object (e.g. structured `{file, line, note}`) rather than the expected `path/file:line` string.

## Suggested fix

- Normalize evidence defensively in `_map_gaps_to_children`: `evidence = r.get("evidence", "")`; `if not isinstance(evidence, str): evidence = str(evidence) or ""` (or json-dumps dicts to salvage file refs).
- Consider the same guard anywhere else evidence is consumed with regex (audit report assembly, gap mapping, child reuse parsing).
- Optionally: strengthen the Phase 2 prompt to require `evidence` be a string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_map_gaps_to_children` (and any sibling evidence consumers) tolerate non-string evidence without crashing.
- [ ] A unit test feeds an AC result with dict evidence and asserts no exception and a sensible (conservative) mapping.
- [ ] Re-running the audit of LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP (or any item whose Phase 2 returns dict evidence) completes and persists.

## Resolution (2026-09-20)

**Status: closed as fixed, per producer decision.**

The bug described in this item was already fixed on `dev` in commit
`1a6539a8` — *"SA-0MSKM2LSP006L0K8: Implementation complete"* (2026-08-15) —
before this intake was run. The commit added the defensive `_evidence_text()`
helper and applied it at `_map_gaps_to_children()` and every other
regex/substring evidence consumer in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
together with six regression tests (dict-evidence gap mapping,
sibling-consumer tolerance, Phase 2 normalisation, end-to-end persist).

**Acceptance criteria status**

- [x] `_map_gaps_to_children` (and sibling evidence consumers) tolerate
  non-string evidence without crashing — done via `_evidence_text()`.
- [x] Unit test feeds an AC result with dict evidence and asserts no exception
  and a sensible (conservative) mapping — done.
- [x] Re-running an audit whose Phase 2 returns dict evidence completes and
  persists — covered by `test_dict_evidence_completes_and_persists`, which
  passes on `dev`.

**Verification:** the six regression tests from commit `1a6539a8` pass on
`dev`; `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlinks to `skill/`, so the installed runner is
identical to the repo copy.

**Producer decision (2026-09-20):** item closed as already-fixed; the
residual debug-log hardening question was answered N/A (out of scope).

# 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — session length & token use vs previous period

## Problem statement

We want empirical evidence on whether instructing agents to "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English" changes agent efficiency. Currently unmeasured. This work item runs a controlled 24-hour experiment: add the instruction to the global AGENTS.md, measure session length and token usage per session over the 24h window, compare against the previous 24h window, then revert.

## Users

- **Operator (Ralph)** — wants to know whether an STE-style output constraint affects session duration and token consumption (cost proxy) before deciding whether to adopt it permanently.

User story:
- As an operator, I want a before/after comparison of session length and token use so that I can decide whether "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." in AGENTS.md is worth keeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Treatment applied and verified:** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) contains exactly the sentence "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." during the experiment window, and is reverted after the window. Both states verified via `grep` (before, during, after).
2. **Baseline metrics computed:** for the 24h period immediately preceding the experiment start (T0), computed from session logs for **all projects**: session count, mean/median session length (minutes), mean/median total tokens per session, input/output/cache breakdown, total tokens, and total cost where recorded.
3. **Experiment metrics computed:** same metrics for the window [T0, T0+24h), sessions attributed to the window by session start timestamp.
4. **Comparison report produced and committed:** delta % and direction for each metric (duration, total tokens, input tokens, output tokens), notable outliers (e.g. sessions with output-token-limit errors), project and model breakdown, and a one-line interpretation per metric. Report lives in the repo (e.g. `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md`).
5. **Reproducible measurement:** a single command re-runs the full analysis over the session-log directory and produces identical results (deterministic). If the measurement is delegated to the proxy's usage tooling, verify that tooling actually exists and runs; otherwise the analysis script in this repo is the source of truth (validated during intake: session logs contain per-message `usage` with input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes (README/wiki entries, code comments in the analysis script).
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (including any tests added for the analysis script).

## Constraints

- **Bare sentence only** — the literal instruction "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." No rule expansion, no dictionary, no enforcement tooling.
- **Global scope** — the change lands in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (affects every project). This is intended; the change MUST be reverted after the window.
- **Do not modify** session logs, proxy configuration, or any other project's files.
- **Measurement scope:** all sessions across all projects (per operator decision).
- STE *compliance* measurement (whether outputs actually follow STE) is **out of scope** — this experiment measures only session length and token use. Any compliance sampling should be a separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- Changes to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` follow the repo's normal workflow: implemented in a worktree, committed to `dev` (never `main`), even though this is a temporary experiment. The symlink `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md → AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` means no install step is needed; the instruction takes effect for sessions *started after* the change lands.

## Existing state

- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (verified).
- Session logs at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` contain: a `session` header event (start timestamp, cwd, id) and per-message assistant events with a `usage` object (`input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `totalTokens`, `cost`). Last event timestamp ≈ session end. Verified during intake.
- Baseline sample (SorraAgents sessions only, 2026-08-09): 69 sessions, ~30.5h total, avg 26.6 min/session, avg 3.8M total tokens/session (dominated by cache reads; total-token values include cache). One extreme outlier session (153 min, 146.9M total tokens) associated with repeated output-token-limit errors — the report must handle such outliers (report both mean and median).
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` exists but currently contains **no source files** (only `__pycache__`). If this is the "existing usage skill in the proxy" intended for measurement, it must be verified to actually run; otherwise the analysis script in this work item is authoritative.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` measures startup-context bytes — related (our change grows startup context by ~50 bytes) but does not measure session token usage. Run before/after to confirm the addition stays within `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` if that gate is enforced.

## Desired change

1. Add the sentence to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in the worktree; commit to `dev`; record exact commit hash and wall-clock T0.
2. Let the experiment run 24h (T0 → T0+24h). No special agent behavior needed during the window beyond normal work.
3. At T0+24h: collect metrics for [T0−24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) across all projects; produce the comparison report; revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (new commit to `dev`); record revert hash.
4. Deliver: report (metrics table, deltas, outliers, interpretation), AC verification, session-log of the experiment itself.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — add then revert the STE sentence (the treatment).
- `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` — comparison report (new).
- `skill/ste100-experiment/scripts/analyze_sessions.py` (new, or revived `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/`) — deterministic analysis over `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl`; produces per-session duration/tokens and window aggregates + tests.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — verify/revive if the proxy-side usage skill is to be used for measurement.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` / `SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR` — "Reduce initial LLM context…" (completed + in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), context-budget angle. Our +1 sentence slightly increases startup context; keep within budget.
- `SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP` (F1) — "Startup-context measurement tooling": produced `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`; related measurement tooling, different axis.
- `SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U` — "Reduce audit skill initial session context size": also touches startup-context surface.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Null result risk:** a bare STE100 sentence may not change model output measurably (no vocabulary enforcement; model may not deeply know STE rules). A null result is a valid outcome — report it as such rather than extending the experiment.
- **Confounds:** session mix (project, work type, human vs automated, model, token-limit error loops) differs between windows; day-of-week/time-of-day effects. - **Boundary sessions:** sessions spanning T0 or T0+24h attributed by *start timestamp* (documented rule).
- **Measurement tooling uncertainty:** if the proxy usage skill is non-functional, the repo analysis script (AC 5) is authoritative — do not block on proxy tooling.
- **Left-over instruction:** the sentence must be reverted; AC 1 greps verify both states. Add a calendar/reminder if available to avoid the window overrunning.
- **Scope creep:** STE compliance scoring, dictionary enforcement, or policy changes are separate work items (`discovered-from:SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD` if created).

All (existing usage skill in the proxy will measure this)". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09. # Intake Brief: Audit runner detects proxy 'cheap' mode and serializes parallelism

## Problem statement

The llm-manager proxy runs in one of two operating modes — **fast** (3-slot local
pool, cloud-backed) or **cheap** (reduced 1-slot local pool). The audit runner
(`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) currently ignores the proxy mode and always
uses its default parallelism (2), so during cheap-mode windows (01:00–10:00 local by
default schedule) an audit that launches concurrent pi child processes races the
single slot: degraded throughput, provider stalls, and concurrency-limit failures.
When multiple audits/dispatchers run at once the race is worse.

## Users

- Audit operators running `audit_runner.py` (item/project audits), and automated
  dispatchers (e.g. the herdr downtime worker's auto-audit dispatches).

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want the runner to automatically serialize
its pi calls when the proxy is in cheap mode, so my audits don't race the single
slot."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At runner start (`main()`, after arg parsing and before any pi call), the runner
   queries `GET <proxy-base>/admin/mode` with a short timeout and parses the JSON
   `mode` field.
2. When the mode is exactly `"cheap"` (case-sensitive), the runner sets **both**
   `AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1` **and** `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` in its own environment
   for this run, and logs a clear detection line to stderr.
3. When the mode is anything else (including `"fast"`), or the query fails
   (unreachable / timeout / non-200 / unparseable), the runner **leaves all
   parallelism settings unchanged** (fail-open) and logs a warning; no verdict or
   status-lifecycle semantics change.
4. `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` is renamed to `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` across code, tests,
   and docs; the legacy name is still honored as a fallback (new name wins).
5. New behavior is covered by unit tests (mocked mode responses: cheap → both env
   vars set to 1; fast → unchanged; query failure → unchanged and warning logged;
   legacy env alias still resolves). Full project test suite passes with the changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and
   `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md` (rename references + new
   cheap-mode behavior described).

## Constraints

- **Read-only:** the runner may only `GET /admin/mode` — never `POST /admin/set-mode`
  (mode switching is operator/herdr territory; the audit mandate stays read-only).
- **Fail-open:** a mode-query failure must never break the audit or add more than the
  short timeout (≈3s) of latency, and must never change verdict semantics.
- **Per-process scope:** the change is `os.environ` on the runner process — it affects
  only this run's spawned pi subprocesses, not other processes or audits.
- **Host-wide semantics preserved:** `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` keeps its host-wide
  flock-semaphore behavior; setting it to 1 in cheap mode caps *this run's* pi
  launches to one at a time (defensive — redundant with `AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1` but
  protects against sibling dispatchers sharing the same ceiling).
- Do not change verdict semantics, the two-phase pipeline, or the freshness gate.

## Existing state

- `audit_runner.py`:
  - `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` env (default 2) → `_resolve_phase2_parallelism()` —
    bounds Phase 1 child screening + Phase 2 child deep-analysis ThreadPoolExecutor
    concurrency (parent call never parallelized).
  - `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env / `--max-concurrency` CLI (default 5) →
    `_acquire_audit_slot()` — host-wide concurrent-pi ceiling via the shared flock
    semaphore (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`, `ENV_MAX_WORKERS =
    "AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY"`); saturated → fail-fast `unmet` unless
    `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` set.
  - `main()` (line ~5706) already wires `--max-concurrency` into `os.environ` before
    dispatch — natural insertion point for the mode query.
- llm-manager proxy (local checkout updated to `dev`, 72a0932; live at
  `http://192.168.0.199:8000`):
  - `GET /admin/mode` → `{"mode": "fast"}` or `{"mode": "cheap"}` (`mode.py`:
    `VALID_MODES = (fast, cheap)`, default fast, persisted in `proxy/.mode`).
  - `POST /admin/set-mode` exists but is out of scope (read-only).
  - Default schedule: cheap 01:00–10:00 local, fast otherwise; manual switches honored
    until next transition.

## Desired change

1. **Rename:** `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` → `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` everywhere
   (constant `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM_ENV` → `AUDIT_PARALLELISM_ENV`), keeping the
   legacy env name as a fallback alias (new name wins; legacy used only when new is
   unset). Update tests + docs.
2. **Mode query at start:** in `main()`, after arg parsing / `--max-concurrency`
   wiring and before command dispatch:
   - Resolve the proxy base URL — new `AUDIT_PROXY_BASE_URL` env var, default
     `http://192.168.0.199:8000` (matches pi's `models.json` "Local Proxy" baseUrl).
   - `GET <base>/admin/mode` with ≈3s timeout; parse `{"mode": ...}`.
   - If mode == `"cheap"`: set `os.environ[AUDIT_PARALLELISM] = "1"` and
     `os.environ[ENV_MAX_WORKERS] = "1"`; print a detection line to stderr.
   - Else (other mode / failure / timeout / non-200 / unparseable): print a warning
     (only on failure) and continue — settings unchanged.
3. **Tests:** mock the mode endpoint (monkeypatch the HTTP client or inject the base
   URL) covering cheap / fast / failure cases; verify env mutation and log lines;
   add a legacy-alias resolution test.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `main()` (mode query + env wiring),
  `_resolve_phase2_parallelism()` + `AUDIT_*_PARALLELISM_ENV` constants (rename +
  legacy alias)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — parallelism resolver tests (rename),
  new mode-query tests (mocked HTTP)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Concurrency / Parallel child deep analysis
  sections (rename + cheap-mode behavior)
- `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md` — rename references
- Reference (external, read-only): `~/projects/llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
  + `proxy/proxy/mode.py` — `/admin/mode` contract

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (completed) —
  notes parallel-Phase-1 was dropped for local-model concurrency limits; same
  concern.
- `SA-0MSAIXTMS003REBW` — Phase 2: parallelize independent child deep-analysis calls
  (P3) (completed) — introduced the parallelism being gated here.
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 2 perf treatment applied to Phase 1 (P7) (completed)
  — Phase 1 child screening also uses this parallelism.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Phase 2 performance evaluation (completed) — flags provider
  concurrency limits for parallel child calls against the local proxy.
- `SA-0MSKB697P000T3HG` — Audit skill: tiered Phase 1 model (fast/cheap model for
  Phase 1 screening) (open, medium) — related cheap-mode theme; separate scope.
- `SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY` — Implement or remove the unimplemented Pre-flight affirmation
  (open, high) — concurrent-audit guard; related, separate scope.
- `SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM` — Fix hardcoded DEFAULT_MODEL 'Proxy/qwen3' in audit runner
  (completed) — proxy model wiring in the runner.
- llm-manager: `LP-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N` (cheap mode keeps remote models enabled),
  `LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6` (mode.py) — the proxy-side mode feature this item consumes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — base URL default:** `AUDIT_PROXY_BASE_URL` defaults to
  `http://192.168.0.199:8000`, matching pi's `models.json` "Local Proxy" entry. If
  the proxy address changes, set the env var (no code change).
- **Assumption — exact match:** mode comparison is exact, case-sensitive `"cheap"`,
  per the request ("If it is anything else leave unchanged").
- **Assumption — fail-open:** a query failure never blocks or alters the audit —
  documented in AC 3.
- **Risk — rename breakage:** external scripts/herdr may set the legacy
  `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`; the fallback alias mitigates. Residual risk: a tool
  that *reads* the env name (none known).
- **Risk — stale mode during run:** the mode can change (or the proxy restart during
  a switch) mid-audit; the runner only checks at start. Accepted — a run sees one
  snapshot; the proxy restart semantics already tell clients to retry.
- **Scope-creep guard:** mode *switching* (`POST /admin/set-mode`), per-call mode
  re-checking, and the tiered cheap model (SA-0MSKB697P000T3HG) are explicitly out
  of scope; record as separate work items if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: How should the runner determine the proxy's current mode? (I found no mode
  endpoint in the older checkout; `/v1/mode` was a 503 catch-all.)
  — Answer (user): `GET /admin/mode`. Source: interactive reply; verified live
  (`{"mode":"fast"}`) and in llm-manager `dev` (handlers.py, mode.py).
- Q: What does `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` do exactly? (Explained: host-wide per-pi-launch
  ceiling via shared flock semaphore, default 5, fail-fast on saturation.) Should
  cheap mode also set it?
  — Answer (user): yes, also set `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: If the mode query fails (unreachable/timeout/unparseable), leave unchanged?
  — Answer (user): OK (fail-open confirmed). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Rename `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` → `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` — keep legacy name as
  fallback or hard-break?
  — Answer (user): rename everywhere, fallback alias OK. Source: interactive reply.
  Research: refs in `audit_runner.py` (5), `test_audit_runner.py` (8),
  `audit-skill-reference.md` (2), `audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md` (2);
  SKILL.md has no name references.
data.title: Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode at start, serialize parallelism for the run

# Enable the context-budget pre-push gate across all framework projects

## Problem statement

Every project that runs the installed pi framework should block a local `git push`
to `dev` when the pi-session startup context surface regresses beyond a
project-appropriate budget. The original rollout plan (2026-08-10) listed six
non-SorraAgents projects, but the framework tooling has since landed and the
project landscape has changed; this intake refreshes the brief to the actual
2026-09-27 state and pins the remaining work.

## Users

- **Framework maintainers** — want a context regression caught locally, before
  it reaches `dev`.
- **Project developers** (e.g. AI_Hell contributors) — should not have to
  remember to run the gate manually.

Example user stories:

- As a framework maintainer, I want every framework project to run the
  context-budget gate on push, so that a skills/AGENTS.md regression cannot
  silently raise session cost across projects.
- As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same pre-push protection as SorraAgents,
  so that my project's startup context does not drift unnoticed.

## Current state (re-verified 2026-10-14; originally verified 2026-09-27)

The original brief's premises are **stale**. The following already landed
(SorraAgents git history):

| Commit | Item | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `6fbc38cf` | SA-0MT1WMPKZ008DL7S | global-symlink fallback for `measure_context.py` in `.githooks/pre-push` |
| `eca4ae60` | SA-0MT1WNWP2007KU7U / SA-0MT1WO815009KXUC | `--generate-thresholds` / `--write-thresholds` in `measure_context.py` |
| `6052e69c` | SA-0MT1WTF170058NJ7 / SA-0MT1WUEIT006U1HC | `install_pi.sh` wires the v2 hook + `core.hooksPath` |
| `3ca016bd` | SA-0MT1WURSU009NAXS | rollout docs in `docs/dev/context-budget.md` |
| `ddc6f6f5` | SA-0MT1WOWAO000T2P1 | hook passes `--repo-root` (global-symlink correctness) |

Project wiring (verified directly):

| Project | hook | `core.hooksPath` | thresholds | In scope? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SorraAgents | v3 (gate + sync + test gate) | `.git/hooks` | yes (15,473 B) | canonical |
| ContextHub | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (1,894 B) | yes |
| dev-scripts | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (371 B) | yes |
| llm-manager | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (967 B) | yes |
| open_source_llm | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (2,048 B) | yes |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (46,807 B) | yes |
| AI_Hell | **v1 (sync only)** | **unset** | **none** (project AGENTS.md = 24,044 B) | **yes — ungated** |
| ampa | v1 (sync only) | unset | none | **no — retired 2026-08-20**; checkout removed from disk 2026-10-14 |

Notes:

- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (§ Rollout to all framework projects) states
  ampa was retired on 2026-08-20 and is out of scope. On 2026-10-14 its
  checkout was moved off disk (`~/.trash/ampa-2026-10-14`); git history is
  intact on `origin` and the local worklog held 0 items, so nothing unique was
  lost. ampa's gate wiring is therefore no longer relevant work.
- The brief's claim that "the global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` is symlinked to all
  projects" is inaccurate: `install_pi.sh` symlinks it to
  `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (machine-global), not into each repo. Consequently
  `measure_context.py` reports `global_agents = 0` and (mostly)
  `skills_prose = 0` in non-SorraAgents repos; each project's gate protects its
  **repo-local** surface, and the global surface is gated by SorraAgents itself.
- AI_Hell is an active framework project (last commit 2026-09-27) with a v1
  hook and no thresholds — a genuine remaining gap under the item title
  "across all framework projects".

## Target outcome

Every in-scope framework project's push to `dev` runs the context-budget gate
with project-appropriate committed thresholds. The only remaining project is
AI_Hell; the rollout is otherwise complete and should be verified end-to-end
before this item is closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: v2 pre-push hook resolves `measure_context.py` from the local repo path
  when present, else the installed global symlink
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`), and stays
  fail-open only when the framework is absent entirely. *(met — `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`)*
- AC2: A repeatable per-project baseline flow emits a committed thresholds file
  (`docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`) for the project.
  *(met — `measure_context.py --write-thresholds`; `tests/test_measure_context.py`)*
- AC3: The v2 hook + gate + `core.hooksPath` are installed in **every in-scope**
  framework project. *(partial — 5 of 5 listed projects done; **AI_Hell
  outstanding**; ampa retired/out of scope)*
- AC4: Worklog sync behaviour is preserved in every project (no v1→v2
  regression). *(met for wired projects — v2 hook contains the sync block)*
- AC5: `scripts/install_pi.sh` propagates the hook/global tooling so future
  projects get the gate automatically, and docs describe the mechanism.
  *(met — `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`; `docs/dev/context-budget.md`)*
- AC6: End-to-end verification: a simulated push in at least one real
  non-SorraAgents framework project fires the gate (blocks an over-budget
  surface, passes a within-budget one). *(unmet — only temp-repo unit tests
  exist; no recorded real-project verification)*
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
  *(pending — refresh rollout table with AI_Hell and the corrected
  global/local measurement note)*
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (pytest + Node),
  including `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`,
  `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`, and
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`. *(pending confirmation)*

## Constraints

- ampa is out of scope (retired 2026-08-20 per `docs/dev/context-budget.md`;
  checkout removed from disk 2026-10-14).
- The gate must remain fail-open when the framework/tooling is absent (old
  worktrees, machines without pi).
- `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is the repo-level wiring mechanism
  (SorraAgents itself uses `.git/hooks`; do not change that without reason).
- Thresholds are generated from a project's own measurement; no shared global
  threshold value.
- Do not add CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Desired change

1. Run `scripts/install_pi.sh` (or the hook-wiring block) in AI_Hell to install
   the v2 `.githooks/pre-push` hook and set `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
2. Generate and commit AI_Hell's own
   `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` from its measurement
   (`--write-thresholds`).
3. Update `docs/dev/context-budget.md`'s rollout table/notes to include AI_Hell
   and correct the global-vs-local measurement statement.
4. Add or record an end-to-end simulated-push verification for one real
   non-SorraAgents project (AI_Hell is the natural candidate).
5. Confirm the SorraAgents full suite is green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/.githooks/pre-push` — replace v1 with v2
  (worklog sync + context-budget gate + branch policy).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` —
  new, generated from AI_Hell's measurement (project_agents ≈ 24,044 B).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/.git/config` — set `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — already wires hooks; verify it runs cleanly in
  AI_Hell (no code change expected).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — rollout table + global/local measurement note.

# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SCANNING block, all phases via _SCANNING_BLOCK)
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` (find-workitem subcommand + module docstring)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_scan_helper.py` (find-workitem tests)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
- `docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md`

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.

# Problem statement

When the implement skill encounters a work item that has already been implemented (e.g. the skill detects a commit where the work was completed but the item is in a wrong state/stage, or an audit identifies gaps in what was done), it should review the most recent audit report, fix any identified gaps inline, and proceed — rather than blindly re-implementing or silently skipping.

## Users

- **Agent executing `/skill:implement <id>`**: needs to handle the "already completed" case deterministically without manual intervention or blind re-implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Detect "already implemented"** — the implement skill recognizes when the work has already been completed (e.g. via commit history, status/stage mismatch, or an audit report indicating prior completion).
2. **Review audit report** — when already implemented is detected, fetch/review the most recent audit report for the item (`/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
3. **Close gaps inline** — if the audit reveals gaps (unmet ACs, failing tests, missed requirements), fix them inline as part of the current item's implementation (option b per intake clarification, 2026-08-13) — NOT by creating new work items.
4. **Skip if clean** — if the audit shows no gaps, report the summary and skip further implementation (no re-work).
5. **Update documentation** — the implement skill's `SKILL.md` is updated to describe this new step and its logic.

## Constraints

- Changes are scoped to `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and corresponding doc hygiene tests.
- No new work items should be created for gaps — they are closed inline.
- Follow the existing implement skill structure (add a numbered step, consistent formatting).

## Existing state

The implement skill has no logic to detect when a work item has already been implemented. It proceeds through all steps regardless, which can lead to redundant work or missed gap remediation when an item's state/stage is out of sync with its actual implementation status.

## Desired change

Add a new step in the implement skill (between Step 3.1 "Definition gate" and Step 4 "Create a worktree") that:
1. Checks whether the item has already been implemented
2. If yes: reviews the latest audit report, identifies gaps, and fixes them inline
3. If no: proceeds to the normal workflow

## Risks & assumptions

- **Detection signal ambiguity** — "already implemented" must be driven by the implement skill's own output (it reports completion with a commit hash), not inferred from status alone; document the exact detection trigger in the skill.
- **Audit staleness** — the most recent audit report may predate later fixes; reuse a fresh audit (same guidance as existing Step 3: reuse a recent audit, else `/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
- **Scope creep in inline gap-closing** — large gaps discovered via audit are potential new work items; keep inline fixes minimal and record extra opportunities as linked work items (discovered-from), not scope.
- **Dependency on audit output format** — logic reads the audit report; keep the reading step aligned with how the audit skill persists reports (`audit_report_<id>.md`).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Add the new step with detection logic and audit review procedure
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — Ensure doc hygiene tests still pass

## Related work

- SA-0MSAS108O009DYKT — audit skill must write audit report files with unique names
- SA-0MPGU5QG40040AWS — Move recent-audit bootstrap into implement skill
- SA-0MPMGES67002AP0Z — Implement per-child audit loop in Ralph

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What counts as 'already implemented'?" — Answer (operator): option d — the implement skill itself sometimes reports the work is already completed and points to a commit hash; in that situation the item is either (a) completed but in the wrong state/stage, or (b) a problem with the implementation was identified in an audit. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.
- Q2: "What does 'close them' (the gaps) mean?" — Answer (operator): option b — fix the gaps inline as part of the current item's implementation, then proceed to in_review. No new work items for gaps. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.

## Problem

The audit runner's merge gate (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) extracts candidate commit SHAs from work-item descriptions and comments using the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b`. This regex incorrectly matches decimal numbers that happen to be composed entirely of hex digits (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` from a test failure message). The numeric sequence after the decimal point (`2329094824319696`, `231051271500847`) is treated as a valid commit SHA, causing false-positive merge-gate failures.

**Example:** A failing test with the error:
```
expected 0.23290948243196963 to be less than or equal to 0.2310512715008475
```
produces candidate commits `2329094824319696` and `231051271500847` from the audit runner, which then fail to integrate into `dev` because they are not real commit SHAs.

## Root Cause

File: `.pi/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, function `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`, line ~6119:

```python
for m in re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

The `\b` word boundary does not prevent matching within decimal numbers. The sequence `0.23290948243196963` is parsed as a decimal literal, but the substring `2329094824319696` (16 hex chars) passes the 7-40 char hex check.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit no longer extracts decimal numbers as commit SHAs:** The regex in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` must not match numeric sequences that are part of decimal literals (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` → no SHA extracted; `2329094824319696` → no SHA extracted).

2. **Valid commit SHAs are still extracted:** The fix must not break extraction of legitimate commit SHAs:
   - Full 40-hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd3cc78f415afca198930339f2138bed218`)
   - Short 7-39 hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd`, `abc1234`)
   - SHAs in commit messages, WL comment text, and work-item descriptions

3. **Commit SHAs prefixed by `#` (GitHub-style) are still extracted:** `#2c15ebd` or `sha=2c15ebd` patterns should still be detected (the `\b` boundary handles `#` as a non-word character, so the hex sequence is still matched).

4. **All existing audit tests pass:** No regression in the existing audit test suite (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/tests/`).

5. **New test coverage:** Add a test that verifies decimal numbers are not extracted as commit SHAs, and a test that verifies valid SHAs in various formats (full, short, GitHub-style) are still extracted.

## Suggested Fix

Replace the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b` with one that excludes decimal-point-adjacent sequences. Options:

**Option A (negative lookbehind for dot):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<!\.)\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?!\.)", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This uses `(?<!\.)` to ensure the match is not preceded by a decimal point, and `(?!\.)` to ensure it is not followed by one.

**Option B (explicit non-digit-dot context):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![0-9.])\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?![0-9.])", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This is more aggressive — it excludes any sequence preceded or followed by digits or dots.

**Option C (split on dots first, then match):**
Preprocess the text: `text.replace('.', ' ')`, then apply the original regex. This is simpler but could break SHAs that happen to be adjacent to dots in unusual contexts (unlikely but possible in commit messages).

**Recommended:** Option A — targeted fix that only excludes decimal-point adjacency, preserving all other behavior.

## Impact

# Intake Brief: Report Use Cases Section

**Problem statement:** The end-of-session report produced by the `render_report` helper
(liaised by intake, implement, plan, and audit skills) currently shows only the skill's
own acceptance criteria (did the skill run correctly?). It does not surface the work item's
own use cases — the acceptance criteria and user stories that define *what* the work is
trying to achieve. Operators scanning reports cannot immediately see what the work item
was about.

**Desired change:** Insert a "Use Cases" section in the canonical report template
immediately after the header line (`**<title>** (<id>)`) and before the headline. This
section lists the use cases / acceptance criteria from the work item being processed.

## Users

- **Operators / producers** who review end-of-session reports in herdr panes — they
  need to see the work item's objectives at a glance alongside the skill's outcome.
- **Agents** (Map, Ralph) that produce reports — they need a simple mechanism to
  extract and render these use cases from the work item description.

## User stories

1. As a producer reviewing a report, I want the work item's use cases displayed
   right after the title so I can quickly understand what the work was about
   without opening the work item.
2. As an agent producing a report, I want a clear, documented way to pass use
   cases into the report renderer so I can include them in my output.
3. As a developer maintaining the report helper, I want the use cases section
   to be optional and gracefully handle cases where no use cases are available.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Use Cases section rendered** — The `render_report()` function inserts a
   `## Use Cases` section between the title line and the headline when use cases
   are provided. When no use cases are provided, the section is omitted entirely
   (no empty heading).
2. **Use Cases rendered as bullet list** — Each use case is rendered as a bulleted
   line (`- <text>`) under the `## Use Cases` heading.
3. **SKILL.md updated** — The canonical report template in `report/SKILL.md`
   documents the new section, its position, and its format. The example rendered
   report includes the section.
4. **Tests updated** — Existing tests in `report/tests/test_render_report.py` are
   updated to account for the new section (section ordering, presence/absence
   of Use Cases depending on whether use_cases are provided).
5. **Backward compatible** — Callers that do not pass use cases see no change
   in output (no empty Use Cases heading). The `use_cases` parameter is
   optional (default `None`).
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The change is in the report helper — a shared dependency of four skills.
  No skill SKILL.md files need procedural changes; the renderer parameter
  is optional so existing callers continue working without modification.
- The use cases are extracted by callers from the work item description
  (typically from an "## Acceptance Criteria" or "## Use Cases" section
  in the description). The renderer itself does not parse descriptions.
- The section must be omitted (not just empty) when no use cases are
  supplied — no orphaned `## Use Cases` heading.

## Existing state

The canonical report template (defined in `report/SKILL.md` and implemented
in `report/scripts/render_report.py`) produces this section order:

```
# Completed <skill_name>
**<title>** (<id>)
<headline>
## Acceptance Criteria  (skill's own AC)
## Meta-Data
## Producer Actions
## Notes
## Conclusion
```

The `render_report()` function accepts: `skill_name`, `work_item_id`, `title`,
`headline`, `acceptance_criteria`, `metadata`, `producer_actions`, `notes`,
`next_action`. The `render_report_from_workitem()` convenience wrapper and
`render_from_wl()` (which calls `wl show`) all route through `render_report()`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Add optional `use_cases` parameter
  to `render_report()` and `render_report_from_workitem()`, insert section
  after title line.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — Update the canonical template and example to
  include the new `## Use Cases` section.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Update tests for the new
  section and test both presence and absence paths.

- **SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR** (self) — This work item.

No questions needed — the work item description is sufficiently clear.
