# Tracer bullet: hermetic-migration recipe + local `git()` wrappers

Parent: SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0

## Goal

Establish the canonical hermetic-git migration recipe end-to-end on the
smallest, lowest-risk helper group (the three local `git()` wrappers), so the
remaining clusters (F2-F5) apply a proven, documented pattern rather than
re-deriving it. This is the tracer bullet: it cuts through code, tests and
docs in one slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The local `git()` helpers in `tests/test_test_cache.py`,
  `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` and `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py`
  are replaced with `shared.git_sandbox` calls (`init_repo`, `commit_all`,
  `run_git`); no bare `subprocess.run(["git", …])` remains in these files.
- [ ] Each migrated repo builder (e.g. `git_repo`, `cache_repo`) has a
  behavioural regression test proving a leaked `GIT_DIR` cannot redirect it —
  the victim repository is unchanged and the fixture repository resolves under
  `tmp_path` — mirroring
  `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py::TestEnvironmentIsolation` and
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py::TestRepoHelpersAreHermetic`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any `docs/dev/` entries such as `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` gains a "Migration recipe" section
  documenting the before/after pattern (factory + injected identity +
  containment assertion) and the regression-test template, so later features
  have a single reference.
- [ ] All existing assertions in the three files pass unchanged (no asserted
  behaviour changes; only the git execution path).

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace the module-level `git()` wrapper in each file with `gs.run_git`, and
  build each throwaway repo with `gs.init_repo(..., default_branch=…)` +
  `gs.commit_all(...)`.
- Add one hermetic regression test per migrated builder, using a victim repo
  and `monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_DIR", …)`, asserting the victim HEAD is
  unchanged and the fixture toplevel is under `tmp_path`.
- Append the migration recipe section to `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_test_cache.py`
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`
- `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py`

None (tracer bullet — must land first).

Its AC1 explicitly names the exact failing tests (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestRunTestsGuardFires::*`, `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py::test_run_tests_spawns_resolved_pytest_when_missing`) and delivers `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` nested-run isolation. 2. **AC2 (guard false positives from external `origin/*` ref movement)** — delivered by **SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8** ("Live-repo guard false-positives on concurrent agent dev fast-forward and worktree churn", completed 2026-10-15). It implemented ownership-based exclusion in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`: refs checked out in registered worktrees other than the guard's own root are excluded, together with their remote-tracking refs (`_remote_tracking_refs_for_branch`) and retained `--track` worktree config (`_retained_worktree_tracked_branches`). End-to-end proofs exist in `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestOwnershipNoFalsePositivesNested` (concurrent `refs/heads/dev` + `refs/remotes/origin/dev` fast-forward stays green at both entry points). The 2026-10-08 teardown ERROR observation (deleted `refs/heads/wl-SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM-…`) predates this fix and is covered by the worktree-removal/register-remove-cycle exclusion tests.

### Residual gap (the only question deciding re-scope vs close)

The literal AC2 wording is "the guard does not fail a run when **only external** `origin/*` refs move". The delivered exclusion is **branch-scoped**: remote-tracking refs are excluded only when they belong to an excluded branch (a branch checked out in another registered worktree). **SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8 explicitly accepted the residual** that a suite running **from the main checkout** still monitors its own `dev`, so a concurrent agent `finish` (fetch + `merge --ff-only` in the main checkout) can still trip a guard armed at the main checkout via `refs/heads/dev` + `refs/remotes/origin/dev` movement.

- **AC3** ("full suite green with ≥3 concurrent agent test runs") is an aggregate/empirical outcome, not a unit-testable deliverable; both fixes target exactly this.

### OPEN QUESTION (single)

Given AC1 and the main-flows of AC2 are shipped, should this item be:

- **(a)** **Closed as superseded** — all reportable root causes delivered by SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 + SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8; the remaining main-checkout guard surface is the operator-accepted residual from SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8.  **Recommended** if you consider that accepted risk already covers the literal AC2 wording.
- **(b)** **Re-scoped to the residual gap** — rewrite ACs to the narrow remaining surface: guard armed at the **main checkout** (or at any root whose own branch is a shared integration branch) must not fail when only another agent fast-forwards `refs/heads/dev`/`refs/remotes/origin/dev`; keep all genuine-mutation detections (config rewrites, working-tree changes, guard-root branch moves caused by the suite).
- **(c)** **Kept open only for AC3 numeric verification** — no new code; use it to track a ≥3-concurrent-run full-suite gate.

**Recommended: (a)**, unless you want the main-checkout `dev` surface closed — in which case (b) with the ownership-exclusion design extended (e.g. treat the main checkout's `dev` remote-tracking ref as churn when the guard root is a worktree, already delivered) and a new decision on the main-checkout-as-guard-root case (currently intentionally monitored to preserve GIT_DIR-leak-class detection, SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX).

Implemented effort-label spelling parity fix (TDD).

Root cause: effort-and-risk skill writes full labels ('Extra Small' ...) via `wl update --effort` (commit c04ecb5b) while wl's canonical vocabulary is abbreviated (XS/S/M/L/XL), so `DEFAULT_AUTOPLAN_EFFORT_SKIP` never matched stored 'S'/'XS' and `PLAN_APPROVAL_EFFORT` never matched stored 'XL'.

Changes (skill/plan/plan_helpers.py):
- Added `normalise_effort_label()` mapping both spellings to the canonical full label (unknown spellings pass through; blank -> '').
- `make_autoplan_decision()`: normalised effort on the idempotence path (the path that runs for already-computed items) and the freshly-computed effort-and-risk path.
- `should_request_plan_approval()`: normalised effort before the AND-gate comparison.

Tests (skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py): normalise_effort_label table, approval-gate abbreviation/full-label parity matrix, autoplan skip parity (idempotence path + plan_if_needed end-to-end 'S'/'XS'+Low -> skip), fresh-path parity, and plan_approval_gate 'XL'+High/Severe -> request_approval. Full suite green (verified via run_tests.py --scope full).

Evidence: `plan-if-needed SA-0MV28WXPA003EHJC` now returns {"decision": "skip", "effort": "Small", "risk": "Low"} (was {"decision": "plan", "effort": "S", ...}).
